summary: Connection churn from many short streams prevents prefetch reuse, causing slot erosion and sustained throughput degradation
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a gradual, sustained drop in dedicated pool throughput over several hours coincident with a high rate of short-lived connections from a single tenant. Impact: AcmeChat's p50 token throughput dropped ~35% and p99 latency increased from ~120ms to ~890ms on their dedicated reservations for several rolling windows. Environment: prod us-east, dedicated pool (reservation-id: res-84f3). Observed: high connection churn (>15k connects/min), unusually high prefetch requests per second, repeated KV cache warmups, frequent small eviction events and GPU-slot fragmentation. Expected: short streams should not starve longer batched work or cause repeated prefetch re-execution that fragments slots. This ticket captures triage, investigation notes, and mitigation attempts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a small dedicated reservation with mixed workloads: 20% steady long-batch traffic (seq len 1024) + 80% short chat streams (avg 4 tokens) from a single tenant.
2) Simulate high connection churn: open/close websocket connections at ~250 RPS per client for 60+ minutes across 100 parallel clients.
3) Observe scheduler allocation churn, repeated prefetch calls in serving-runtime, and falling p50 throughput on the dedicated pool dashboards.
4) Capture metrics from /metrics and /debug endpoints for prefetch_requests_total, evictions_total, gpu_slot_free_fraction.
5) Re-run with client-side keepalive (30s) to compare behavior — mitigation is expected if churn is root cause.
logs: [2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] prefetch: tenant=acmechat req_id=8f7cd prefetch_start seq_id=312 ttl_ms=60000
[2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] scheduler: allocate slot gpu=gpux012 reservation=res-84f3 reason=short_stream
[2026-03-10T15:03:11Z] nvlink: peer-drop detected on gpux012 (kernel 0xffff) — transient IO errors, correlates with eviction spikes
observed_metrics: p50 throughput baseline: 12k tokens/s -> degraded to 7.9k tokens/s over 2 hours
prefetch_requests_total: increased 5x from baseline during the incident window
gpu_slot_free_fraction: dropped from 0.28 -> 0.05 during sustained churn
evictions_total: saw periodic spikes aligned with connection bursts
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: a dominant tenant generating a high volume of very short streams causes repeated prefetch attempts and frequent allocation/eviction cycles, which fragment GPU slots (slot erosion) and reduce effective batch sizes for other tenants. Support validated correlation between tenant X (AcmeChat) connection churn and pool-level degradation via dashboards: dedicated-reservation res-84f3. SRE captured serving-runtime traces showing prefetch_start events for conversation keys that are immediately abandoned when clients disconnect; these prefetches still consume slot attachments and KV cache warm-up GPU memory until eviction. Autoscaler reacts to transient drop in usable slots by attempting re-provisioning which amplifies allocation churn.
hypotheses_tested: A: Churn causes prefetch re-execution -> confirmed by matching request ids and kv-cache misses
B: Autoscaler thrash increases fragmentation -> partially confirmed: autoscaler made 2 scale-down attempts in-window which coincided with additional eviction events
C: Underlying GPU IO errors (nvlink) are the root cause -> inconclusive; transient nvlink peer-drops observed but not clearly causal — further kernel-level logs requested from infra team
workarounds_attempted: 1) Temporary tenant throttling applied at edge to limit short-stream connect rate (reduced churn by ~60%) — immediate throughput improvement observed
2) Increased prefetch TTL to 2 minutes in the serving-runtime for this reservation to allow reuse across reconnects — reduced repeated warmups but increased short-lived memory hold times
3) Applied server-side keepalive guidance to customer SDK (recommended 30s) — pending customer rollout
4) Pinning the workload to a separate dedicated reservation as isolation short-term mitigation
comments: Support (Asha): Asked customer for sample request ids, connection patterns, and traffic start/end timestamps.
Customer (AcmeChat - James Lee): Provided sample traffic trace and confirmed they launched a new client version yesterday that reduces connection pooling (likely cause).
SRE (Miguel): Collected serving-runtime heap profiles and scheduler allocation timeline; nvlink peer-drops seen but only during highest eviction windows. Attached metric snapshots to ticket.

Engineer (Priya Shah): Noted a known scheduler behavior where prefetch holds a slot attachment until KV warmup completes — suggested short-term TTL tuning and a medium-term scheduler change to avoid holding attachments for clients that disconnect quickly.
Support (Asha): Recommended customer enable client keepalive and provided SDK snippet; scheduled a call for 2026-03-11 to coordinate mitigation rollout.
next_steps: 1) SRE to gather kernel-level NVMe/NVLINK logs for gpux012 during the incident window (assigned to Miguel). 2) Engineering to prototype scheduler change that cancels prefetch attachments if client disconnects within X ms (PR sketch: runtime/prefetch-cancelation). 3) Customer to roll out client-side keepalive and connection pooling update; monitor p50/p99. 4) Consider short-term tenant isolation if churn persists.
resolution: In Progress - partial mitigations applied (tenant throttling and increased prefetch TTL). Awaiting customer SDK rollout and infra kernel logs to confirm or rule out hardware IO contribution. Follow-up actions: scheduler patch (PR linked), postmortem if repeats.
postmortem_followup_items: Add a dashboard tile showing prefetch_active_count alongside connects/min per tenant
Add autoscaler hysteresis for dedicated reservations experiencing high short-lived-connection churn
Implement runtime prefetch cancellation on client disconnect (engineering task)
Customer-facing best-practice doc for connection pooling and recommended keepalive settings
